If you planned service for Madrid’s Búhos night buses, which months would you prepare for heavier demand?

## Boardings dip every August

The data count boardings across routes N1–N24, which connect Cibeles with Madrid’s neighborhoods. This notebook embeds the monthly totals and runs offline with the course R packages.

The totals sum all time bands for route codes 501–524 by calendar month, from January 2022 through September 2026. The archive was updated September 29, 2026 and the current-year file October 15, 2026. [Archive and current data](https://datos.emtmadrid.es/es/dataset/demanda-diaria-viajeros-autobus) · [Route codes](https://datos.emtmadrid.es/dataset/lineas-emt) · [November 2023 service change](https://www.emtmadrid.es/Noticias/EMT-Madrid-pone-en-marcha-la-nueva-linea-%E2%80%98buho%E2%80%99-N3.aspx)

Contains data from EMT Madrid’s Daily Bus Ridership, accessed November 26, 2026 and available under the Open Data Commons Attribution License. [Powered by EMT de Madrid](https://www.emtmadrid.es/) · [Data license](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/by/1-0/)

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Boardings rise from 2022 through 2026 and dip every August. A vertical line marks the November 2023 service change."

source_note <- "Powered by EMT de Madrid · Nov 26, 2026"
chart_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

rides |>
  autoplot(Boardings) +
  geom_point(data = rides |> filter(month(Month) == 8),
             aes(x = Month, y = Boardings), colour = "#1261A0", size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = yearmonth("2023 Nov"), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey45") +
  scale_x_yearmonth(breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(subtitle = "August (dots)\nNov 2023 service change (dash)",
       x = NULL, y = "Monthly boardings (thousands)", caption = source_note) +
  chart_theme
```

## Where do the fitted values miss?

Fit through September 2025. Both models damp the trend. `A,Ad,A` uses additive errors and seasonality. `M,Ad,M` uses multiplicative errors and seasonality.

```{r}
train <- rides |> filter(Month < yearmonth("2025 Oct"))
test <- rides |> filter(Month >= yearmonth("2025 Oct"))

fit <- train |>
  model(
    `A,Ad,A` = ETS(Boardings ~ error("A") + trend("Ad") + season("A")),
    `M,Ad,M` = ETS(Boardings ~ error("M") + trend("Ad") + season("M"))
  )

fit |>
  tidy() |>
  filter(term %in% c("alpha", "beta", "gamma", "phi")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) |>
  transmute(Model = .model, alpha, beta_star = beta / alpha, gamma, phi) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5, col.names = c("ETS", "α", "β*", "γ", "φ"))
```

Read α for level, β* for trend, γ for seasonality, and φ for damping. Fable reports β, so the table uses β* = β / α. The small β* and γ values mean new observations barely revise the slope and seasonal pattern. Both φ estimates are close to fable’s default upper bound of 0.98. [Fable’s ETS reference](https://fable.tidyverts.org/reference/ETS.html)

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Monthly observed-minus-fitted errors for both models, with a horizontal zero line and the same scale in both panels."

fit |>
  augment() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = .resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55") +
  geom_line(colour = "#26364A") +
  facet_wrap(vars(.model), ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_yearmonth(breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(subtitle = "Fitting errors through Sep 2025",
       x = NULL, y = "Observed − fitted (thousands)", caption = source_note) +
  chart_theme
```

## Which forecast comes closer over the next 12 months?

Forecast all 12 months from September 2025, then compare with the boardings EMT observed.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Solid observed counts and two dashed forecast series for October 2025 through September 2026. Both models miss by the most in June 2026."

test_fc <- fit |> forecast(h = 12)

test |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Boardings), colour = "#26364A", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = as_tibble(test_fc),
            aes(y = .mean, colour = .model, linetype = .model),
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("A,Ad,A" = "#1261A0", "M,Ad,M" = "#A34C14")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("A,Ad,A" = "dashed", "M,Ad,M" = "dotdash")) +
  scale_x_yearmonth(breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b %y") +
  labs(subtitle = "Observed boardings (solid line)\nVertical axis starts above zero",
       x = NULL, y = "Monthly boardings (thousands)",
       colour = "ETS", linetype = "ETS", caption = source_note) +
  chart_theme
```

```{r}
training_scores <- fit |> accuracy() |> select(.model, `Training RMSE` = RMSE)
test_scores <- test_fc |> accuracy(test) |> select(.model, `Held-out RMSE` = RMSE)

fit |>
  glance() |>
  select(.model, AICc) |>
  left_join(training_scores, by = ".model") |>
  left_join(test_scores, by = ".model") |>
  rename(ETS = .model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Model comparison. RMSE is in thousands of boardings.")
```

Training RMSE scores one-step-ahead fitted values. Held-out RMSE scores months 1 through 12 from the same forecast date. Which months account for the larger misses?

## What should EMT plan for over the next year?

Among these two models, both AICc and held-out RMSE favor `ETS(A,Ad,A)`. Re-estimate it using data through September 2026. Which months look busiest, and how wide is the 95% prediction interval?

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Observed boardings through September 2026 and a monthly forecast through September 2027 with a shaded 95 percent prediction interval."

final_fit <- rides |>
  model(`A,Ad,A` = ETS(Boardings ~ error("A") + trend("Ad") + season("A")))

final_fit |>
  forecast(h = 12) |>
  autoplot(rides |> filter(Month >= yearmonth("2024 Oct")), level = 95) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = yearmonth("2026 Oct"), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey45") +
  scale_x_yearmonth(breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  guides(fill_ramp = guide_legend(title = "Prediction interval")) +
  labs(subtitle = "Forecast starts in Oct 2026",
       x = NULL, y = "Monthly boardings (thousands)", caption = source_note) +
  chart_theme
```
